issues.description: The solution repository's PersonService uses a method named registerParent(Person, Person) while the template, REST resource, and tests expect a method named addParent(Person, Person). This name/signature mismatch between PersonService and the rest of the code (PersonResource and unit tests) is a structural inconsistency that will prevent the project from compiling and confuses students about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name/signature across artifacts. Rename registerParent(Person, Person) in PersonService to addParent(Person, Person) (preserving the implemented logic and return type), or add a public addParent(Person, Person) method that delegates to registerParent. Ensure the method signature exactly matches what's declared/used in the template, PersonResource and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and template define and refer to a PersonService method named addParent(Person, Person), but the solution's service implementation uses the name registerParent(Person, Person) instead. Other solution artifacts (PersonResource and the tests) still call addParent. This inconsistent naming makes it unclear which method students should implement or call and can lead to compilation/test failures or extra cognitive load mapping the requirement (addParent) to the implemented method (registerParent).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's registerParent method to addParent(Person person, Person parent) to match the problem statement, template, and tests (or add a forwarding addParent method that delegates to registerParent). Ensure all references (PersonResource, tests, and any documentation) consistently use addParent.
